key_insight: Picard–Chebyshev weakly nonlinear analysis predicts how streak–planar-wave interactions generate oblique and harmonic waves whose amplitudes control the onset of streak breakdown.
engineering_relevance: Predicting finite-amplitude transition triggers could inform strategies to delay turbulence in channel flows.
method: Formulate weakly nonlinear optimal perturbation analysis for compressible parallel flows using Picard–Chebyshev iteration.
Track non-modal amplification and nonlinear interactions across an expanding set of wavenumber components.
Systematically refine predictions from linear dynamics toward DNS behavior in the weakly nonlinear regime.
evidence_signal: For subcritical plane Poiseuille flow at Mach 0.3 and Reynolds number 3000, the abstract reports high agreement with DNS and identifies a planar-wave optimal perturbation that triggers streak breakdown in full nonlinear simulation.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the reported flow conditions, and tracking an expanding set of interacting wavenumbers may increase computational cost.
paper_title: Predicting trigger in streak breakdown via Picard-Chebyshev approach in plane-Poiseuille flow
